page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m8.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual instance provisioned via the KVM hypervisor. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores via symmetric multithreading. Memory allocation is generous at 64 GB of RAM, establishing a high 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 8 GB per virtual core. Cache architecture features 32 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX and AVX-512F alongside standard cryptographic acceleration via AES. The instance contains no integrated local storage and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network throughput without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest CPU throughput coupled with stable memory subsystem behavior. Single-core performance shows limitations across several benchmarks, scoring 920.0 in Geekbench and 1105.89 in stress-ng, reflecting the conservative 2.5 GHz clock profile. Multi-core performance scales proportionally to 3502.0 in Geekbench and 5855.73 in stress-ng, while overall PassMark CPU performance registers in the average bracket at 6861.03. In uncached memory bandwidth operations, the system achieves 38.27 GB/sec read and 35.69 GB/sec write throughput. High-throughput operations, such as Redis SET handling at 5.79 million operations per second and static web serving at 4.15 GB/sec, fall into the lower quartiles relative to modern compute profiles.

Cost efficiency for this instance is rooted in its memory density rather than raw compute throughput. Because single-thread and compute-heavy benchmarks lag behind newer architectures, relying on this server for processor-intensive operations presents an efficiency tradeoff. Furthermore, the absence of local disks demands network-attached block storage for persistent data. This hardware profile functions most effectively when handling memory-resident datasets, in-memory caching with Redis, medium-sized relational databases, and data staging pipelines where memory capacity is the primary constraint.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m8.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor, the instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading and a 33 MB L3 cache. It pairs these compute resources with 64 GB of system memory, yielding an expansive 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server includes no bundled local storage, necessitating reliance on remote block volumes, and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Without hardware acceleration from GPUs, computing performance is modest; Geekbench and stress-ng tests place single-core and multi-core throughput in lower percentiles, while PassMark results register average multi-core efficiency. Consequently, this configuration delivers cost efficiency primarily through large RAM capacity per vCPU rather than raw processor power, making it appropriate for in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, and background ETL processes that prioritize memory footprint over compute speed.
